<!-- openclaw:security-sensitive-guard -->

### ⚠️ Security sensitive changes

This maintainer PR changes sensitive security components.

**No secops approval is required. This comment is informational because the PR author has Maintain or Admin access.**

- Current SHA: `e8d35e47e902ddc91fab28938beb44b0004d1b7d`
- Maintainer: @steipete
- Repository role: `admin`

These security sensitive changes were made:

- `src/agents/sandbox/context.ts`: Controls sandbox containment or tool execution authority. Check filesystem and network isolation, approval scope, and command allowlists.
- `src/agents/sandbox/workspace-mounts.ts`: Controls sandbox containment or tool execution authority. Check filesystem and network isolation, approval scope, and command allowlists.

Carefully review these changes before merging.

Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. ## What this changes This PR creates missing managed skill directories before selecting read-only sandbox mounts. **Example:** A new writable sandbox starts with no host skills or .agents/skills directories. - **Before:** The missing sources are omitted, allowing writes under /workspace/skills. - **After:** Preparation creates the directories so mount selection includes read-only skill overlays. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | The focused implementation has no identified code defect, but security-boundary and upgrade evidence is incomplete. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Real behavior proof is necessary before merge. See [Before merge](#before-merge). | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Security review found an item that needs attention. | ## Product **Kind:** Bug fix · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** A newly started writable sandbox can modify skill paths because their absent host directories receive no read-only overlays. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored direction addresses a concrete protection gap, preserves ordinary workspace writes, and reuses existing preparation and mount owners. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 4 items remain** Keep open: this maintainer-authored PR addresses the linked first-launch protection gap through the existing workspace and mount owners; no discrete introduced code defect was found. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `e8d35e47e902ddc91fab28938beb44b0004d1b7d` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add real behavior proof** - Authority-chain proof required: supplied tests exercise real directory preparation and mount selection with mocked surrounding services, but do not show a newly launched Docker or Podman sandbox rejecting protected-path writes while allowing ordinary writes, or released/reassigned custody preventing the new mkdir effects; provide redacted terminal output or logs without credentials or private endpoints. After adding proof, update the PR body, then request a new review with `@clawsweeper re-review`. The PR author or someone with repository write access can request it. - [ ] **Resolve security review attention item** - No concrete introduced bypass was found, but final-effect authority evidence remains incomplete. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk** - The PR owner must establish that released or reassigned workspace custody prevents the newly introduced host-directory mutations before filesystem I/O. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - The review found that existing stored data may not work after upgrade. Show that existing data still loads and works with this change. ## Findings None. ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: Supply first-launch container write-rejection evidence, final-effect custody-revocation evidence, and a latest-stable upgrade with retained workspace data and container recovery.
Agent review details ### How this fits together Sandbox preparation consumes the selected workspace, access mode, and lifecycle authority, then supplies protected filesystem sources to container and filesystem-bridge mount selection. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Selected workspace and authority] --> B[Workspace preparation] B --> C[Guarded skill directory creation] C --> D[Canonical mount selection] D --> E[Container mount plan] D --> F[Filesystem bridge policy] E --> G[Protected skill paths] F --> G ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep creation in workspace preparation, retain the shared validator and filesystem authority guard, and verify first-launch protection plus existing-container recovery. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Current main omits absent skill directories from protected mounts, matching the linked Docker reproduction; this read-only review did not execute target code. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The patch is a focused repair using existing owners: preparation materializes shared candidates, while mount resolution remains validation-only and retains containment checks. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [ab705c5790a6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ab705c5790a6db8fcc505590c4ce6d75898e67b6). ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Prove the final filesystem effects (recommended)** The PR owner should show allowed workspace preparation succeeding and revoked or reassigned custody rejecting directory creation before any host mutation. ### Provenance checked - `Absent skill roots` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85591: Existing skill instructions were protected while absent roots intentionally retained normal workspace write behavior.) - `Materialized skills workspace` keeps the original intent (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90798: Non-workspace skills must be readable through sandbox-owned read-only projections without overwriting user project content.) - `Private workspace protection` keeps the original intent (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/135702: Private workspaces support ordinary coding while protecting their own managed instructions without exposing the shared agent workspace.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security Needs attention: No concrete introduced bypass was found, but final-effect authority evidence remains incomplete. ### Evidence What I checked: - **Pinned patch and existing ownership:** The introduced patch shares candidate selection between preparation and validation, invokes preparation after skill sync, and retains canonical containment and leaf-symlink filtering. ([`src/agents/sandbox/workspace-mounts.ts:106`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8d35e47e902ddc91fab28938beb44b0004d1b7d/src/agents/sandbox/workspace-mounts.ts#L106), [e8d35e47e902](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e8d35e47e902ddc91fab28938beb44b0004d1b7d)) - **Current main retains the reported path:** Current main filters absent skill sources out of protected mounts and returns from skill synchronization without creating those sources. ([`src/agents/sandbox/workspace-mounts.ts:42`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ab705c5790a6db8fcc505590c4ce6d75898e67b6/src/agents/sandbox/workspace-mounts.ts#L42), [ab705c5790a6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ab705c5790a6db8fcc505590c4ce6d75898e67b6)) - **Original behavior was deliberate:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85591 explicitly preserved writes beneath absent skill roots; this maintainer-authored repair explains changing that behavior to protect first launch. ([`src/agents/sandbox/workspace-mounts.ts:42`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1b7bf4a56f9c92c0ddb78b26f547a13e4f25996d/src/agents/sandbox/workspace-mounts.ts#L42), [1b7bf4a56f9c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1b7bf4a56f9c92c0ddb78b26f547a13e4f25996d)) - **Credited replacement and concrete report:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/94425 supplies the missing-directory Docker scenario; https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96028 was closed unmerged and its maintainer discussion identifies this PR as the credited continuation of momothemage's work. - **Supplied proof and enforcement:** The full body reports red/green filesystem regressions but explicitly excludes native first-launch Docker or Podman proof; the security guard says no separate SecOps approval is enforced for this maintainer PR. ([e8d35e47e902](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e8d35e47e902ddc91fab28938beb44b0004d1b7d)) - **Existing-container recovery boundary:** New protected sources change the effective mount plan; a hot retained container with different mounts is preserved and rejected with a recreate command. ([`src/agents/sandbox/current-config.ts:32`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8d35e47e902ddc91fab28938beb44b0004d1b7d/src/agents/sandbox/current-config.ts#L32), [e8d35e47e902](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e8d35e47e902ddc91fab28938beb44b0004d1b7d)) ### PR surface Source +71, Tests +64. Total +135 across 4 files. Added test files: 0.

### Root-cause cluster Relationship: `fixed_by_candidate` Canonical: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/94425 Summary: This PR implements the first-launch missing-source repair tracked by the security report and continues the closed original candidate. Members: - `canonical`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/94425 - Its missing-host-directory scenario is the exact behavior repaired by this patch. - `superseded`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96028 - The maintainer explicitly identifies this PR as its credited replacement. Proposal only: this assessment does not dispatch repair, suppress jobs, mutate sibling items, close, or merge anything. ### Labels Label changes: - add `P1`: The linked report and current source establish missing first-launch read-only protection on executable skill directories. - add `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`: Previously absent roots become protected mounts, which can change custom-bind selection and require recreation of retained containers. - add `merge-risk: 🚨 security-boundary`: The patch adds host filesystem mutations during preparation and changes when sandbox skill write restrictions take effect. - add `rating: 🦪 silver shellfish`: Overall readiness is 🦪 silver shellfish; proof is 🦪 silver shellfish and patch quality is 🦐 gold shrimp. - add `status: 📣 needs proof`: The PR needs real behavior proof before ClawSweeper can clear the contributor ask. Label justifications: - `P1`: The linked report and current source establish missing first-launch read-only protection on executable skill directories. - `merge-risk: 🚨 security-boundary`: The patch adds host filesystem mutations during preparation and changes when sandbox skill write restrictions take effect. - `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`: Previously absent roots become protected mounts, which can change custom-bind selection and require recreation of retained containers. - `rating: 🦪 silver shellfish`: Overall readiness is 🦪 silver shellfish; proof is 🦪 silver shellfish and patch quality is 🦐 gold shrimp. - `status: 📣 needs proof`: The PR needs real behavior proof before ClawSweeper can clear the contributor ask. ### Rank-up moves Optional improvements that raise the rating; they are not merge blockers. - Show first-launch protected-path write rejection through the real container runtime while ordinary workspace writes succeed. - Prove released or reassigned workspace custody prevents the new host-directory mutations before I/O. - Verify a latest-stable upgrade preserves workspace contents and handles retained containers whose mount plans change. ### Rating scale 6/6 🦀 challenger crab · 5/6 🦞 diamond lobster · 4/6 🐚 platinum hermit · 3/6 🦐 gold shrimp · 2/6 🦪 silver shellfish · 1/6 🧂 unranked krab. Overall follows the weaker of proof and patch quality; ✨ marks media proof (a screenshot, video, or linked artifact) that directly shows the changed behavior. ### Workflow ClawSweeper edits this one comment on every review.
